react_result.final_narrative_text: The ten differentially abundant metabolites converge on two tightly coupled metabolic hubs. Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260 / hsa00260) is the top cross-paradigm winner, hit simultaneously by RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR 8.6e-17), MetaboAnalystR KEGG-ORA (p 3.3e-07), and Mummichog m/z-direct activity (p 0.0024). Methionine Metabolism (KEGG:map00270 / hsa00270) is the second convergent hit, enriched across RaMP (FDR 1.1e-14), MetaboAnalystR (p 0.0006), and Mummichog (p 0.011). Both pathways share S-adenosylmethionine (SAM), L-cysteine, L-serine, glycine, adenosine, and choline as driver metabolites, consistent with coordinated one-carbon metabolic flux perturbation. In the glycine-serine-threonine node, glycine and L-serine act as entry and interconversion substrates linked through serine hydroxymethyltransferase; L-threonine contributes additional carbon input; choline supplies methyl groups via betaine. In the methionine node, SAM is the central methyl donor whose synthesis from methionine and adenosine directly consumes adenosine, while its catabolism generates homocysteine which is converted to cysteine through the transsulfuration pathway — explaining the simultaneous cysteine signal. The folate cycle bridges both hubs: serine donates one-carbon units to 5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolate, which ultimately regenerates methionine for re-methylation to SAM, constituting a coupled cycle of methyl-group generation and consumption. The independent detection of 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde (a dopamine/tyrosine catabolite) in the tyrosine metabolism node (Mummichog, p=0.045) suggests a secondary perturbation of catecholamine catabolism. Together these changes indicate a treatment-induced rewiring of one-carbon/methyl donor metabolism with downstream consequences for methylation capacity, redox homeostasis (via cysteine for glutathione synthesis), and connected amino acid interconversion.

react_result.final_narrative_text: The RaMP ORA identified Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260) as the strongest cross-tool winner, with 7 of 10 input metabolites as members (glycine, L-serine, L-threonine, L-cysteine, S-adenosyl-L-methionine, choline, adenosine; FDR = 8.6e-17). Mummichog confirmed the same node independently (p = 0.003), and additionally surfaced Methionine and cysteine metabolism (p = 0.010) as a second coherent hit. Within that second node, methionine adenosyltransferase catalyzes S-adenosyl-L-methionine synthesis from methionine and adenosine, while cystathionine beta-synthase mediates the homocysteine-to-cysteine conversion, explaining both the SAM and L-cysteine signals. Glycine participates in the serine hydroxymethyltransferase reaction (glycine + 5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolate ↔ serine + tetrahydrofolate), providing one-carbon units for methyl-group metabolism. Choline supplies methyl groups through betaine-dependent remethylation, feeding the same SAM-generating cycle. 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde was independently detected by Mummichog in Tyrosine metabolism (MUMM:tyrosine_metabolism, p = 0.048) and is established in the literature as a dopamine catabolite (PMID 41517809). Sucrose is not enriched in any amino-acid pathway and maps instead to sialic acid / sugar metabolism as a peripheral carbohydrate signal.
